messages:
Eli Torres: heads-up — I found a class of requests where the routing looked correct in the gateway but the decision log entry is missing the header-override metadata. repro attached below.

Nadia Chen: oh interesting, did you check sampling flags? could be sampling dropped the decision log before we attach the override details.

Eli Torres: sampling appears to be false on the decision_log proto in several examples. but the access logs show X-Route-Override present and the request actually got routed to the overridden model.

Jorge Ramos: can you paste one of the raw gateway traces? if sampling happened earlier in the pipeline we might be trimming fields.

Eli Torres: pasted one minimal trace. snippet:```
TRACE id=8f3a1b route=/v1/generate headers={host:api.redwood, x-route-override:rdw-gptq} decision_log.sample=false routing.target=rdw-gptq
```

Lin Wu: that decision_log.sample=false is the crux. our sampling decision runs in the routing prefilter currently, before header normalization and header-derived annotations are attached. if we sample-out we never record the later override metadata.

Samir Patel: hmm that implies any header-based routing override will be invisible in decision logs for sampled-out requests. That'll skew metrics and make debugging impossible for low-sampled traffic.

Nadia Chen: two ways to fix: 1) move sampling decision after override attachment so sampled decisions include overrides, 2) when sampling happens early, persist a minimal 'override-candidate' flag to the decision envelope that follows through. option 2 is less invasive but brittle.

Jorge Ramos: agree. patch idea: add a tiny bitfield to the initial envelope (pre-normalize) called override_hint which is set if X-Route-Override header exists. sampling can still happen early but decision-log exporter will include override_hint if sampled-in. if sampled-out we still won't have full meta but at least we can estimate prevalence.

Eli Torres: alternative is to bias sampling upward for requests that include override header (always sample those). that avoids missing these cases completely. downside is it skews sampling distribution and increases cost.

Lin Wu: we should also consider the UX: override headers are a debugging tool for support teams. I'd prefer guarantee that override events are visible in decision logs rather than relying on hints. moving sampling is cleaner.

Samir Patel: operational ask — can we flip gate to 100% sample for the gateway for 20m while we gather data? we'll need metrics and a quick rollback. @deploy-bot can you schedule a short sampling-gate run if we get a thumbs-up? :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled rollout: sampling-gate=100% on cluster gateway-prod from 2026-03-18T14:05Z for 20 minutes. will notify in #incidents if rollout fails.

Nadia Chen: thanks. next steps I propose: (1) collect the 20m samples and measure how many override cases lacked decision detail, (2) prototype moving sampling decision to post-normalize (small PR), (3) if risk is too high fallback to override_hint approach as a stopgap.

Jorge Ramos: I'll open a draft PR for the sampling-after-normalize change and benchmark latency impact. tagging @Lin and @Nadia for review.

Eli Torres: great. I'm adding a tiny test to our route-fuzzer to assert that request with X-Route-Override always produce a decision_log containing either override metadata or override_hint. that'll help prevent regressions.

Samir Patel: thanks team. let's sync after the 20m capture. :eyes:
